findings.title: task 1.1: load/loadMore/retry resolve before the request settles
findings.detail: Task 1.1 says a no-op call 'settles with the request in flight (if any)', which implies the method promises follow the request. Instead load(), loadMore() and retry() call start() and return Promise.resolve() at once, so `await list.load()` returns while the state is still `loading`, and a no-op call made while a request is in flight resolves at once instead of waiting for it.
findings.suggested_fix: Make start() return the promise chain of the request (pending.then(...)), keep it as the in-flight promise, and have load/loadMore/retry, including their no-op paths, return that promise or Promise.resolve() when nothing is in flight.

findings.title: load() promise settles before the page arrives
findings.detail: No scenario says when the promise returned by load() settles. The committed code resolves it immediately; an implementation that resolves after the page is applied would behave differently.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN `load()` is awaited on an idle list whose request is still unanswered THEN the promise resolves at once and `getState().status` is `loading`.

findings.title: subscribe calls the listener immediately on sign-up
findings.detail: subscribe() calls the listener once synchronously before registering it, even though nothing changed. This is not in the task text, and it differs from a store that notifies only on changes.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN a listener is passed to `subscribe` THEN it is called once at once, before any state change, and again for every later change.

findings.title: A failed first page moves focus to the retry button
findings.detail: focusAfterChange returns `retry` for any loading→error change, including the first page (no items). Design says 'a first page moves no focus', which a reader could apply to a failed first page as well. The scenarios only pin a failed load more.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN `focusAfterChange` gets (`loading` with no items, `error` with no items) THEN it returns `retry`.

findings.title: mapEnvelopeErrors gives __proto__ an own key when the caller lists it
findings.detail: fieldNameOf only checks `fields.includes(name)`. If the caller's field list contains "__proto__", then body/__proto__ is set as an own enumerable `__proto__` key through defineProperty. Another implementation could reject the name with isFieldName.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN `mapEnvelopeErrors` gets fields `["__proto__"]` and an entry `body/__proto__` "x" THEN the result has an own enumerable `__proto__` key with "x" and its prototype is unchanged.

findings.title: A query key present with value undefined is refused
findings.detail: cursorPageFetcher refuses a query that has `limit` or `cursor` as an own key even when its value is undefined (QueryValue allows undefined). The scenario pins only `{ limit: 5 }`.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN `cursorPageFetcher` gets `query: { limit: undefined }` THEN creation throws `KitError` `KIT_PROP_INVALID`.

findings.title: task 3.2: stacked Field puts the error before the control
findings.detail: Task 3.2 orders the stacked field as label, hint, control, error. Field.tsx renders label, then hint and error together, then the control, so the error comes before the control.
findings.suggested_fix: In the stacked layout render label, hint, children(control), then the error paragraph.

findings.title: task 2.1: checkbox uses --ui-color-accent, outside the listed colour roles
findings.detail: Task 2.1 and design Decision 8 limit colours to the listed roles and to pairs that CONTRAST_PAIRS covers. .ui-checkbox uses accent-color: var(--ui-color-accent), which is not among them. The token is defined, since the token test passes.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop accent-color, or confirm that --ui-color-accent on bg is a pair CONTRAST_PAIRS covers.

findings.title: task 1.2: parseCursorPage accepts non-plain objects
findings.detail: Task 1.2 says parseCursorPage accepts a plain object. The code accepts any object that is not an array, such as a class instance or one with inherited items. The implementer's note says it parses with Object.hasOwn checks, but it does not.
findings.suggested_fix: Check that Object.getPrototypeOf(body) is Object.prototype or null, and read items and next_cursor through Object.hasOwn.

findings.title: task 1.1: load/loadMore/retry resolve before the request settles
findings.detail: Task 1.1 says a no-op call 'settles with the request in flight (if any)', which implies the method promises follow the request. Instead load(), loadMore() and retry() call start() and return Promise.resolve() at once, so `await list.load()` returns while the state is still `loading`, and a no-op call made while a request is in flight resolves at once instead of waiting for it.
findings.suggested_fix: Make start() return the promise chain of the request (pending.then(...)), keep it as the in-flight promise, and have load/loadMore/retry, including their no-op paths, return that promise or Promise.resolve() when nothing is in flight.

findings.title: load() promise settles before the page arrives
findings.detail: No scenario says when the promise returned by load() settles. The committed code resolves it immediately; an implementation that resolves after the page is applied would behave differently.
evidence:
web/src/kit/data/cursor-list.ts: load(): Promise<void> { ... start(null, true);
      return Promise.resolve();
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN `load()` is awaited on an idle list whose request is still unanswered THEN the promise resolves at once and `getState().status` is `loading`.

findings.title: subscribe calls the listener immediately on sign-up
findings.detail: subscribe() calls the listener once synchronously before registering it, even though nothing changed. This is not in the task text, and it differs from a store that notifies only on changes.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN a listener is passed to `subscribe` THEN it is called once at once, before any state change, and again for every later change.

findings.title: A failed first page moves focus to the retry button
findings.detail: focusAfterChange returns `retry` for any loading→error change, including the first page (no items). Design says 'a first page moves no focus', which a reader could apply to a failed first page as well. The scenarios only pin a failed load more.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN `focusAfterChange` gets (`loading` with no items, `error` with no items) THEN it returns `retry`.

findings.title: mapEnvelopeErrors gives __proto__ an own key when the caller lists it
findings.detail: fieldNameOf only checks `fields.includes(name)`. If the caller's field list contains "__proto__", then body/__proto__ is set as an own enumerable `__proto__` key through defineProperty. Another implementation could reject the name with isFieldName.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN `mapEnvelopeErrors` gets fields `["__proto__"]` and an entry `body/__proto__` "x" THEN the result has an own enumerable `__proto__` key with "x" and its prototype is unchanged.

findings.title: A query key present with value undefined is refused
findings.detail: cursorPageFetcher refuses a query that has `limit` or `cursor` as an own key even when its value is undefined (QueryValue allows undefined). The scenario pins only `{ limit: 5 }`.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN `cursorPageFetcher` gets `query: { limit: undefined }` THEN creation throws `KitError` `KIT_PROP_INVALID`.

findings.title: task 3.2: stacked Field puts the error before the control
findings.detail: Task 3.2 orders the stacked field as label, hint, control, error. Field.tsx renders label, then hint and error together, then the control, so the error comes before the control.
findings.suggested_fix: In the stacked layout render label, hint, children(control), then the error paragraph.

findings.title: task 2.1: checkbox uses --ui-color-accent, outside the listed colour roles
findings.detail: Task 2.1 and design Decision 8 limit colours to the listed roles and to pairs that CONTRAST_PAIRS covers. .ui-checkbox uses accent-color: var(--ui-color-accent), which is not among them. The token is defined, since the token test passes.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop accent-color, or confirm that --ui-color-accent on bg is a pair CONTRAST_PAIRS covers.

findings.title: task 1.2: parseCursorPage accepts non-plain objects
findings.detail: Task 1.2 says parseCursorPage accepts a plain object. The code accepts any object that is not an array, such as a class instance or one with inherited items. The implementer's note says it parses with Object.hasOwn checks, but it does not.
evidence: web/src/kit/data/page-fetcher.ts: if (typeof body !== "object" || body === null || Array.isArray(body)) {
findings.suggested_fix: Check that Object.getPrototypeOf(body) is Object.prototype or null, and read items and next_cursor through Object.hasOwn.

findings.title: DataTable Load more button has no key and the stub comment remains
findings.detail: In the actions array the Load more element has no `key` while retry has one, so React warns. DataTable.tsx still starts with the scaffold 'Signature stub' comment.

findings.title: task 4.1: an enum without a type is rejected instead of being an enum field
findings.detail: Task 4.1 says the enum kind has `type` absent or "string". parseProperty returns 'the property has no type' for every property without `type` before any enum handling, so `{ enum: ["a", "b"] }` becomes unsupported and blocks the form.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat a property with `enum` and no `type` as kind `enum` before the missing-type check.

findings.title: A property without a type loses its name and label
findings.detail: The unsupported field for a property with no type gets name "" and the label 'Field <i+1>' even when the property name is valid (for example `c`). The user cannot tell which property is unsupported, which works against 'never drop a property silently'. Task 4.1 asks for the blank-name label only when a name fails isFieldName and is blank.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN a property with a valid name has a schema object without `type` THEN its `unsupported` field has `name` "" and `label` "Field <i+1>", with i its index.
